(by the IDBI Act, 1964) | hq_location = IDBI Tower, [[World Trade Centre, Mumbai|WTC Complex]], [[Cuffe Parade]] | hq_location_city = [[Colaba]], [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]] | hq_location_country = India{{cite web |title=Contact Us |url=https://www.idbi.bank.in/contact-us.asp |website=IDBI Bank |access-date=29 January 2019}} | key_people = {{Unbulleted list|TN Manoharan ([[Chairman|Part Time Chairman]] & [[Independent director|Independent Director]])||Rakesh Sharma ([[Managing director|MD]] & [[CEO]])}} | products = {{ubl|[[Investment banking]]|[[Commercial banking]]|[[Retail banking]]|[[Asset Management]]|[[Pensions]]|[[Mortgages]]|[[Credit cards]]}} | brands = | services = | revenue = {{Increase}} {{INRConvert|30370|c}} (2024) | operating_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|9774|c}} (2024) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|5763|c}} (2024) | assets = {{Increase}} {{INRConvert|467386|c}} (2026) | equity = {{Increase}} {{INRConvert|40320|c}} (2024) | num_employees = 20,078 | num_employees_year = September 2024 | owner = [[Life Insurance Corporation of India]] (49.24%)
[[Government of India]] (45.5%){{cite news |title=Govt, LIC together may dilute up to 65% stake in IDBI Bank |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/govt-lic-together-may-dilute-up-to-65-stake-in-idbi-bank-8883991.html |access-date=22 October 2022 |work=Monet Controlsendwesternunion |language=en}} | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = {{Unbulleted list|IDBI Capital Markets & Securities|IDBI Intech|IDBI Asset Management|IDBI MF Trustee Company|IDBI Trusteeship Services{{cite web |title=IDBI Group |url=https://www.idbi.com/idbi-group.asp |website=IDBI Bank |access-date=29 January 2019}}}} | module = | ratio = 13.31% | rating = | website = {{Url|https://idbi.bank.in}} | footnotes = }} '''Industrial Development Bank of India''' or '''IDBI''' is a [[Scheduled Commercial Bank]] under the ownership of [[Life Insurance Corporation of India]] (LIC) and [[Government of India]]. It was established by [[Government of India]] as a wholly owned subsidiary of [[Reserve Bank of India]] in 1964, IDBI as a [[development finance institution]], which provided financial services to industrial sector. In 2005, the institution was merged with its subsidiary commercial division, IDBI Bank, and was categorised as "Other Public Sector Bank" category. Later in March 2019, [[Government of India]] asked LIC to infuse capital in the bank due to high [[Non-performing loan|NPA]] and capital adequacy issues and also asked LIC to manage the bank to meet the regulatory norms. Consequent upon LIC acquiring 51% of the total paid-up equity share capital, the bank was categorised as a 'Private Sector Bank' for regulatory purposes by [[Reserve Bank of India]] with effect from 21 January 2019. IDBI was put under Prompt Corrective Action of the Reserve Bank of India and on 10 March 2021 IDBI came out of the same. At present direct and indirect shareholding of [[Government of India]] in IDBI Bank is approximately 95%, which Government of India (GoI) vide its communication F.No. 8/2/2019-BO-II dated 17 December 2019, has clarified and directed all Central/State Government departments to consider IDBI Bank for allocation of Government Business.{{Cite web|last=Gupta|first=Arindam|date=25 August 2021|title=Tumultuous journey of a development bank|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/opinion/tumultuous-journey-of-a-development-bank/article36103013.ece|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210828155634/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/opinion/tumultuous-journey-of-a-development-bank/article36103013.ece|archive-date=28 August 2021|access-date=10 January 2022|website=[[Business Line]]}} Many national institutes find their roots in IDBI like [[SIDBI]], [[Exim Bank of India|EXIM]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.eximbankindia.in/|title=Home - Exim Bank|website=www.eximbankindia.in}} [[National Stock Exchange of India]], [[SEBI]], [[National Securities Depository Limited]]. Presently, IDBI Bank is one of the largest Commercial Banks in India. As of July 2025, the bank has an aggregate balance sheet size of ₹4,11,661.{{cite web |url=http://www.idbi.com/idbi-bank-about-us.asp |title=About us |publisher=IDBI Bank |access-date=22 February 2014}} It also has more than 2,100 Banking branches and more than 3,700 ATMs.{{Cite web |title=Personal & Corporate Banking {{!}} MSME & Agri banking - IDBI Bank |url=http://www.idbibank.in/err404.aspx |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=www.idbibank.in}} 24 banking outlet- fixed BC, spreading all over India as of July 2025, including one overseas branch in [[Emirate of Dubai|Dubai]]. It operates 58 e-lounges {{As of|2023|8|1|lc=y}}.{{cite web|url=https://www.idbibank.in/branch-atm.asp |title = IDBI Bank Branch & ATM Locator|publisher=IDBI Bank |access-date=1 February 2020}} {{As of|2021|9}}, [[Life Insurance Corporation|LIC]] holds the majority stake in this bank having 49.24% shareholding and the [[Government of India]] holds 45.48%, with LIC being in control of the management of the bank. ==History== ===Overview of development banking in India=== {{Unreferenced section|date=January 2022}} Development Banking emerged after the [[Second World War]] and the [[Great Depression]] in the 1930s. The demand for reconstruction funds for the affected nations compelled in setting up of national institutions for reconstruction. At the time of Independence in 1947, India had a fairly developed banking system. The adoption of bank dominated financial development strategy was aimed at meeting the sectoral credit needs, particularly of agriculture and industry. Towards this end, the [[Reserve Bank of India|Reserve Bank]] concentrated on regulating and developing mechanisms for institution building. The commercial banking network was expanded to cater to the requirements of general banking and for meeting the short-term working capital requirements of industry and agriculture. Specialized Development Financial Institutions (DFIs) such as the IDBI, [[NABARD]], [[National Housing Bank|NHB]] and [[SIDBI]] were set up to meet the long-term financing requirements of industry and agriculture. ===Formation of Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)=== {{Unreferenced section|date=January 2022}} The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) was established in 1964 under an [[Act of Parliament]] as a wholly owned subsidiary of the [[Reserve Bank of India]].{{Cite web |date=16 May 1964 |title=The Industrial Development Bank Of India Act, 1964 |url=https://indiankanoon.org/doc/1403851/ |access-date=6 January 2026 |website=Indian Kanoon}}{{Cite web |title=Issues relating to Industrial Development Bank of India Limited |url=https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/732292/1/9766.pdf |access-date=6 January 2026 |website=Parliament Library, [[Parliament House, New Delhi|Sansad Bhavan]]}} In 1976, the ownership of IDBI was transferred to the Union government and it was made the principal financial institution for coordinating the activities of institutions engaged in financing, promoting and developing industry in India. IDBI provided financial assistance, both in rupee and foreign currencies, for green-field projects and also for expansion, modernization, and diversification purposes. In the wake of financial sector reforms unveiled by the government since 1992, IDBI also provided indirect financial assistance by way of refinancing of loans extended by State-level financial institutions and banks and by way of rediscounting of bills of exchange arising out of the sale of indigenous machinery on deferred payment terms.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} After the public issue of IDBI in July 1995, the government shareholding in the bank came down from 100% to 75%. IDBI played a pioneering role, particularly in the pre-reform era (1964–91), in catalyzing broad-based industrial development in India in keeping with its government-ordained 'development banking' charter.{{Promotion inline|date=January 2026}}
Some of the institutions built with the support of IDBI are the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]], [[National Stock Exchange of India]], the [[National Securities Depository Limited]], the [[Stock Holding Corporation of India Limited]], the Credit Analysis & Research Ltd, the Exim Bank (India), the [[Small Industries Development Bank of India]] and the [[Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India]]. ===Conversion of IDBI into a commercial bank=== A committee formed by RBI recommended the development financial institution (IDBI) to diversify its activity and harmonize the role of development financing and banking activities by getting away from the conventional distinction between commercial banking and developmental banking. To keep up with reforms in financial sector, IDBI reshaped its role from a development finance institution to a commercial institution. With the ''Industrial Development Bank (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act'', 2003, IDBI attained the status of a limited company viz., IDBI Ltd.{{Citation needed|date=January 2022}} Subsequently, in September 2004, the [[Reserve Bank of India]] incorporated IDBI as a 'scheduled bank' under the ''RBI Act, 1934''. The commercial banking arm, IDBI Bank, was merged into IDBI in 2005. === Direct government intervention === The merger was expected to streamline operations of the bank. However, IDBI continued to base its policy towards industrial sector like the erstwhile IDBI entity did. This resulted in the retail business of the bank to be limited to 13 percent of its total business. {{As of|2018|3}}, the total [[Non Performing Assets (NPA)]] rose to {{INRConvert|55588|c|lk=on|year=2018}} and were about 28 percent of its total loans. This was the highest among Indian banks. The Union government intervened, with [[Life Insurance Corporation]] bailing out the bank with an infusion of {{INR|9300}} crores. On 29 June 2018, LIC got a technical go-ahead from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to increase stake in IDBI Bank up to 51%.{{cite news|date=29 June 2018|title=IRDAI clears LIC IDBI Bank Deal|newspaper=[[The Economic Times]]|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/irdai-clears-lic-idbi-bank-deal-issuer-to-invest-rs-10000-13000-crore-in-tranches/articleshow/64795569.cms|access-date=1 July 2018}} LIC completed the acquisition of 51% controlling stake on 21 January 2019, with a total investment of {{INR|21624}} crores.{{Cite news|date=21 January 2019|title=LIC completes acquisition of 51% stake in IDBI Bank|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/lic-completes-acquisition-of-51-stake-in-idbi-bank/articleshow/67621734.cms|access-date=11 January 2022}}{{Cite news|last=K.|first=Ram Kumar|date=8 March 2021|title=LIC holds the key in Govt's IDBI Bank stake sale|work=[[Business Line]]|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/lic-holds-the-key-in-govts-idbi-bank-stake-sale/article34016850.ece|url-status=live|access-date=11 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423150930/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/lic-holds-the-key-in-govts-idbi-bank-stake-sale/article34016850.ece|archive-date=23 April 2021}} == Operations == ===Acquisition of United Western Bank=== In 2006, IDBI Bank acquired [[United Western Bank]] (headquartered at [[Satara district|Satara]]) in a rescue. By acquiring UWB, IDBI Bank doubled the number of its branches from 195 to 425.{{cite web |url=http://www.idbi.com/idbi-bank-history.asp |title=History |publisher=IDBI Bank |access-date=22 February 2014}}{{cite news |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2006/sep/12bank.htm |title=United Western Bank to merge with IDBI |newspaper=Rediff.com |date=13 September 2006 |access-date=22 February 2014}} === Strategic disinvestment to LIC === LIC of India completed the acquisition of 51% controlling stake in the bank in January 2019, making it the majority shareholder. Subsequent to the enhancement of equity stake by LIC of India, Reserve Bank of India has clarified via press release on 14 March 2019, that IDBI Bank stands re-categorised as a private sector bank, with retrospective effect from 21 January 2019. LIC took over the management control of the bank while the Union government, categorised as a promoter.{{Cite news|date=19 September 2021|title=IDBI Bank strategic sale: Most merchant bankers indicate 52 weeks' time|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/idbi-bank-strategic-sale-most-merchant-bankers-indicate-52-weeks-time/articleshow/86338225.cms|access-date=11 January 2022}} ==Listings and shareholding== IDBI Bank's equity shares are listed on [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and the [[National Stock Exchange of India]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bseindia.com/stock-share-price/idbi-bank-ltd/idbi-bank/500116/ |title=IDBI Bank|publisher=BSEindia.com |access-date=22 February 2014}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nseindia.com/live_market/dynaContent/live_watch/get_quote/GetQuote.jsp?symbol=IDBI |title=IDBI Bank |publisher=NSE India |access-date=22 February 2014}}{{Update inline|date=February 2022|reason=Update what happened after LIC takeover}} {{As of|2025|9|30}}, the Union government held 45.48% shares in IDBI Bank, while LIC held 49.24% and the remaining is held by non-promoters. ==Employees== As of 1 September 2023, the bank had 18,283 employees, out of which 197 were employees with [[disability|disabilities]].{{cite web |url=http://www.idbi.com/pdf/annualreport/Anual-Report-2012-2013-07082013.pdf |title=Annual Report 2012-13 |publisher=IDBI Bank |access-date=22 February 2014}} The average age of bank employees on the same date was 34 years.
